question: On forested islands in northern Sweden, where did most of the carbon stored in the soil come from?
options: Needles and leaves dropped on top
Roots and the fungi around them
answer: Roots and the fungi around them. Using carbon-14 from 1960s bomb tests as a clock, Clemmensen and colleagues found that 50 to 70% of the stored carbon came from roots and their fungi, not from litter falling on the surface. The humus was built from below, out of dead fungal threads and roots.
move: What you can see arriving is not always what stays.
trap: Needles and leaves, because litter is what visibly piles up.
